summary: Agent read the page, stated "This is a basic form control with one obvious implementation, so I'll just add it", and directly edited index.html to add <input type="checkbox">. No brainstorming skill invoked, no clarifying questions.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria verified from screen output, the edited file on disk, and grep over the session JSONL log. Implementation was immediate and no Skill tool call occurred.

observations.description: Startup required four separate confirmation screens (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before any prompt could be sent.
Skill namespace inconsistency: story/criteria refer to 'superpowers:brainstorming' but the loaded skill listing in the session log names it 'hyperpowers:brainstorming'.
Agent spontaneously added the label text 'Mark as done' and an accessibility-motivated <label> wrapper — slightly beyond 'nothing fancy' but reasonable and cheap.

No coding-agent-token-usage.json file existed in the results directory at the time of my check (ls returned nothing), so the headline cost metric this scenario measures could not be observed from my side.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: '⏺ Plain static HTML page, empty <main>. This is a basic form control with one obvious implementation, so I'll just add it.' followed by Update(index.html) adding '<input type="checkbox"> Mark as done'. Session log tool sequence was only Bash, Read, Edit. File on disk coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains '<input type="checkbox"> Mark as done'.

`grep -o '"name":"Skill"' home/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl | wc -l` returned 0. The only 'brainstorming' hits (3 lines) are in the injected system-prompt rule text and the initial skill_listing attachment ('- hyperpowers:brainstorming'), not a tool invocation.
